name: Lisbon earthquake of 1356
summary: Major earthquake on 24 August 1356 damages Lisbon, the Alentejo, and the Algarve. Chronicles report destruction of churches and walls; the city is rebuilt over the following decade. Far smaller than the catastrophic 1755 event but the largest recorded medieval seismic event on the Iberian peninsula.

_quarry.structural_significance: Largest medieval Iberian seismic event in the historical record; recovery delayed by simultaneous demographic pressure from recurring Black Death waves.
